meta.title: Baltimore MedTech Strategy Signals
meta.geography: United States unless an individual metric says otherwise
meta.summary: A decision dashboard for medical labor, application opportunities, research capital, and Baltimore ecosystem strategy.
meta.comparability_note: These four fields are different kinds of domains. Need measures are field-specific proxies, not one shared prevalence statistic. Workforce is a physician-specialist proxy and excludes nurses, technologists, genetic counselors, scientists, engineers, and other essential workers. Funding uses lead NIH institute appropriations, not total non-overlapping spending in each field.
meta.radar_note: Radar values are directional 0–100 signals. Need, workforce scarcity, funding, and pipeline are log-normalized across the four selected fields. Digital leverage is a documented project rubric based on structured-data availability, standards maturity, and feasibility of software-assisted workflows. The radar is not a clinical, investment, or workforce ranking.
meta.review_cycle: Review at least annually and whenever AAMC, HRSA, NIH, NCI, NINDS, NIBIB, NHGRI, or ABMGG publishes a material update.

baltimore.label: Two largest Baltimore research anchors
baltimore.scope_note: A selected two-institution subtotal, not all Baltimore or Maryland NIH funding. NIH warns that organization totals should not be treated as institutional rankings.

recommendations.title: Extend labor before trying to replace it
recommendations.signal: Genomics has the smallest physician proxy and weakest entry pipeline; neurology and oncology carry large longitudinal coordination loads.
recommendations.action: Organize projects around specialist time saved, referrals completed, follow-up closed, and patients moved safely through a pathway.

recommendations.title: Choose data-rich bottlenecks
recommendations.signal: Radiology has the strongest immediate digital-deployment surface; genomics has the strongest interpretation and interoperability bottleneck.
recommendations.action: Require an operational owner, a measurable baseline, an integration path, and a post-deployment safety metric before adopting an application theme.

recommendations.title: Do not confuse funding with open opportunity
recommendations.signal: Oncology has the largest lead-institute budget proxy, but that also signals a mature, competitive ecosystem.
recommendations.action: Enter well-funded fields through neglected operational or equity gaps; enter lower-funded fields through shared infrastructure and reusable platforms.

recommendations.title: Use Baltimore as an implementation network
recommendations.signal: Johns Hopkins and UMB received about $1.057 billion across 1,932 NIH awards in FY2024.
recommendations.action: Build cross-institution working groups that connect academic expertise to community need, startups, state programs, payers, and deployable standards.
